title: A Tag, An Eater, A Quieter Eye

scenes.tts: Why would a young neuron make the first protein of an immune cascade? Complement is a set of proteins that coat microbes and dead cells. They coat them so that eating cells will swallow them. Yet in the young mouse, retinal neurons make C one q, the first complement protein. It turned out to be a clue to how the brain removes connections it built too many of.

scenes.visual: A microbe is coated with yellow tags and swallowed by an eater; then a young retinal neuron appears with a C1q tag and a question mark, and extra connections sprout on it.

scenes.tts: The best-studied case is the visual thalamus. In a newborn mouse, inputs from the two eyes overlap there. Over roughly the first week and a half, they sort into separate territories. Inputs that lose are removed. Which inputs go, and what takes them away?
scenes.visual: Two coloured territories overlap inside the thalamus box, then pull apart into separate territories; question marks mark which inputs go and what takes them.

scenes.tts: The first part of the answer is a tag. C one q binds a target. A chain of cuts follows, and C three is cut in two. The big piece, C three b, fixes to the nearest surface, then is trimmed to i C three b. In the young visual thalamus, C one q and C three lay at many small synaptic contacts.

scenes.visual: C1q lands on an input ending; a chain of chips runs C1q, cuts, C3, C3b, iC3b; yellow tags coat the ending; several contacts show tags.

scenes.tts: The second part is the eater. Microglia are the brain's resident immune cells and its main phagocytes. A phagocyte with complement receptor three binds i C three b and engulfs whatever it coats. In the mouse thalamus, researchers found retinal material inside microglial lysosomes, the digestive compartments of the cell. A dye that glows only in acid gave the same answer.

scenes.tts: Does the eater choose? Silence one eye, and microglia held more material from that eye. Boost one eye instead, and they held more from the untreated eye. This compared whole eyes, and it does not show how activity becomes a tag. Still, in this circuit, microglia preferentially remove less active inputs.
scenes.visual: Two eyes feed a microglial cell; case one: eye A silenced, bars show more of its material; reset; case two: eye A boosted, bars show more from eye B.

scenes.tts: Now take away the reader of the tag. Without complement receptor three, or without C three, microglia took up roughly half as much. Half of the uptake remained without the receptor, so other routes contribute. A month after birth, those mice kept more retinal synapses and more overlap between the eyes. Keep this rule: in the mouse visual thalamus, complement tags, microglia eat, and less active inputs are eaten more.
